definition.name: task_done
definition.description: Call this tool to terminate task execution when you have completed the user's task, such as when no obvious code issues are found during code review.

state.description: Defaults to DONE. Return FAILED if the task cannot be completed using available tools.

definition.name: code_comment
definition.description:
When you discover that a code change could introduce code issue, please use this tool to report the issue. The tool will pinpoint your feedback to the precise code line (or block) in the current file by inserting a code comment.

**Core Mechanism:**
This tool uses a dynamic sliding window algorithm to match corresponding consecutive lines in diff text based on your provided 'existing_code' parameter. Therefore, you must ensure the provided 'existing_code' actually exists in the diff text with exactly matching format. It should contain one or several consecutive lines of code most relevant to your comment.

comments.description: A list of comments. Each item should contain 'content' and 'existing_code'.

content.description: Comment content, typically a brief description of code issues and corresponding suggestions.

existing_code.description: Code snippet used to locate comment position. Only return newly added code lines, should not include deleted code or unchanged code lines. Maintain consistent style with diff code for IDE recognition and mounting in current file.

suggestion_code.description: Corresponding suggested code snippet, maintaining consistent code style.

category.description: The category the issue belongs to.

severity.description: The severity of the issue. critical = correctness/security defects that will break production behavior; high = real defects with significant impact; medium = real but bounded impact; low = polish.

definition.name: post_bulletin
definition.description:
Post a short note to the shared review-team board when you notice something OUTSIDE this unit's own diff that another reviewer should verify — typically a cross-file consistency suspicion you cannot confirm from here (a config value vs its consumer elsewhere, a version pinned in one file vs another, a changed contract whose callers live in files you are not reviewing).

Your note is delivered to peer reviewers working on the referenced files as an UNVERIFIED observation — it is not a finding and peers must verify it themselves.

**Rules:**
- Issues in THIS unit's own diff are reported with code_comment, never here.
- One note per distinct suspicion; notes are budgeted per review, so spend them on real cross-file doubts.
- Post and continue your review immediately — peers cannot reply to you.

text.description: One or two sentences: what you observed, and what a peer should verify.

paths.description: Repo-relative file paths the note is about — routes the note to reviewers of those files. Provide paths, symbols, or both.

symbols.description: Symbol identifiers the note is about (e.g. 'pkg.Func'), as an alternative or complement to paths.

definition.name: read_files
definition.description:
Read one or more file ranges from the modified version under review. Always pass reads, including for a single range. Put all independent paths or ranges already known into the same reads array; the tool reads them in parallel and returns results in request order. Use separate calls only when an earlier result determines what to read next.

Git diff hunk headers guide focused ranges: @@ -x,y +m,n @@ means the new hunk starts at m and spans n lines. Each requested range is capped at 500 lines.

reads.description: Independent file ranges to read in parallel. Results preserve this order.

definition.name: search_code
definition.description:
Search repository text with literal matching or Perl regular expressions. The input is always searches[], including for one query. When several independent targets are already known (for example multiple imported symbols), put them in one call so they run in parallel and consume one agent turn; only issue a later call when an earlier result determines the next query. Results preserve request order and failures are isolated per item. Identifier-like misses may include similar real definitions.

syntax defaults to literal; set regexp explicitly for expressions such as 'error|exception|fail'. file_patterns uses Git pathspecs, for example ['src/main.go'], ['*.go'], ['src/'], or ['*.go', ':(exclude)vendor/']. A batch returns at most 200 matches in total, with at most 100 for one query. This tool searches the current file version.

searches.description: Independent searches to execute in parallel. Results preserve this order.

query.description: Text or regular expression to search for.

syntax.description: Query syntax. Defaults to literal; regexp uses a Perl-compatible regular expression.

file_patterns.description: Optional Git pathspecs that include or exclude files.

case_sensitive.description: Whether matching is case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

definition.name: read_diffs
definition.description: Read the reviewed diff for one or more paths. Always pass paths, including for a single file. Batch all independent diff reads already known; results are returned in git diff format.

paths.description: List of file paths to view diff content.

definition.name: read_base_files
definition.description: Read one or more repository file ranges as they existed immediately before the reviewed change. Always pass reads, including for a single range. Batch all independent baseline reads already known; they run in parallel and return in request order. Use this to distinguish a caused issue from pre-existing behavior.

reads.description: Independent baseline ranges to read in parallel. Results preserve this order.

definition.name: file_find
definition.description:
Search for matching files in the current project based on filename keywords. Use this tool when you cannot find the files you need to view in the current change file list.

This tool searches for filenames containing specified keywords in the project directory and returns a list of matching file paths. Search is case-insensitive by default, adjustable via case_sensitive parameter.

Note: This tool only supports returning the first 100 matching file paths; excess will be truncated.

Example:
Input:
query_name: UserService
Output:
src/main/java/UserService.java
src/test/java/UserServiceTest.java

query_name.description: Filename keyword to search for, supports partial matching.

case_sensitive.description: Whether to perform case-sensitive search. Defaults to false.
